about: The three ancient dragons who serve the King of Dragons (order 95: only three; D-193): Ash, Frost and Storm, hand-written, each a full profile, one of a kind in the bestiary. Validated by tools/lint-figures.mjs.

category.name: The Ancient Dragons
category.note: Only three ancient dragons live: Ash, Frost and Storm, who serve the King of Dragons and keep his hall while he sleeps.

figures.name: Ashgar

skills.does: A fire white at its heart, lit only in the King's name.

items.does: A claw of the King's own, shed in the first age. It opens the hall under the Wyrmcrown.

goals.why: to keep the King's hall and hoard until he wakes

grudges.why: the Saint struck the King down on the Saint's Stair
Vaskareth, the King's eldest, gives herself airs above his servants

story: The Ancient Ash Dragon, eldest of the three who serve the King of Dragons. It keeps the King's hall under the Wyrmcrown while he sleeps.
The lesser dragons keep out of its sky.
It has gone down into the hall and seen the King. The wound has not closed in sixty years, and Ashgar is afraid.

figures.name: Rimewing

skills.does: A winter that comes in a day, over a whole valley.

items.does: A shard of the glacier the King sleeps under; it never melts.

goals.why: to keep the ice over the King's hall whole
to keep the lesser dragons to the King's old laws

grudges.why: the White Winter's ice creeps toward the King's

story: The Ancient Frost Dragon, the second of the three who serve the King. It sleeps in the ice where the King sleeps under the stone.
It knows the elder dragons are counting the years, and that some of them hope the King never wakes.

figures.name: Galeheart

skills.does: A storm called down on one place and held there.

items.does: Stones of hail that circle its head and never fall.

goals.why: to keep the other dragons to their own skies
to be the one who finishes the fight on the Saint's Stair, if the King cannot

grudges.why: Stormwing will not keep to the skies the King gave her

story: The Ancient Storm Dragon, the strongest of the three who serve the King. It keeps the roads of the sky and the other dragons to their own.
It has climbed the Saint's Stair at night and watched the old man sleep. It did not strike.
